Park Medi World 

CMP: 282

P/E: 43.9

Park Medi World Limited, which runs the Park Group of Hospitals, has just set up a brand new company that it owns completely. This new company is called Park Medicity Prayagraj Limited, and it officially came into existence on September 8, 2026.

The reason they created this new entity is to build and run a large hospital in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. This will be a 550 bed multi super speciality hospital, meaning it will offer many different medical specialities under one roof.

Interestingly, this hospital project has come through a public private partnership, which means the local municipal corporation in Prayagraj has awarded this project to Park Medi World to build and operate the hospital, rather than the government building it entirely on its own.

Since Park Medi World owns one hundred percent of this new company, there is no conflict of interest here. No related parties or group companies have any special stake in this deal, and everything has been done at arm's length, meaning fairly and without favoritism.

The amount of money involved to start this new subsidiary is quite small at this stage, only about fifteen lakh rupees, used to buy one lakh fifty thousand shares in the new company. This is essentially just the initial seed capital needed to officially register the new entity. 

The bigger investment for actually building the hospital would likely come later.

This move signals that Park Medi World is expanding its footprint beyond its existing markets into a new and significant city. 

Prayagraj is a major religious and administrative hub in Uttar Pradesh, known for large events like the Kumbh Mela which draw enormous crowds, so a large modern hospital there could serve a very large population base that may currently lack access to advanced medical care.

Winning a public private partnership project is also meaningful because governments usually award such contracts only to companies they consider financially capable and credible, so it can be seen as a vote of confidence in Park Medi World's ability to execute large scale healthcare projects. 

Successfully completing this one could also make it easier for the company to win similar hospital contracts in other cities in the future, creating a template for growth through government partnerships rather than only through fully self funded new hospitals.

From a business perspective, once operational, a 550 bed hospital adds a large amount of new bed capacity to the company's overall network, which over the years should translate into a meaningful boost to revenue and profits as the hospital ramps up patient volumes. It also allows Park Medi World to diversify geographically, reducing its dependence on its current cities and giving it a foothold in a fast growing part of Uttar Pradesh.

However, since actual construction, government approvals, staffing, and eventually filling up hospital beds with patients typically take several years, the real financial benefit from this move will likely show up gradually over the coming years rather than immediately. 

In short, this is a long term growth seed being planted today, positioning the company for expanded scale and geographic reach in the healthcare sector over the next several years.

WHY HEALTHCARE CAN BE INTERESTING
The interesting part of healthcare is that revenue can be repeat in nature, depending on the business.

▪️ Hospitals → patients continuously require treatments, procedures and healthcare services.

▪️ Diagnostics → tests are performed repeatedly, creating recurring demand.

▪️ Pharma → chronic therapies and regularly prescribed medicines can provide repeat business.

▪️ Medical devices & consumables → many products are consumed or require replacement, creating repeat demand.

▪️ CDMO / contract manufacturing → once a company develops a relationship with a customer, repeat orders can potentially create long-term revenue visibility.

▪️ Healthcare platforms & services → established customer/patient networks can create recurring usage and stronger operating leverage as the business scales.

But recurring revenue doesn't automatically mean a good investment.

We still need to check the quality of the revenue, margins, cash flows, debt, working capital, customer concentration, regulatory risks, promoter quality and valuation.

Healthcare can be a very powerful compounding sector - but only when the underlying business, execution and valuation all make sense.

So don't just look at which stock has gone up.
Study the business. Track the execution. Research the numbers. Then take a decision.

HFCL FY26 Annual Report Key Takeaways 🧵

• Strong FY26: Revenue grew 21.8% to ₹4,949 Cr, EBITDA +63.2% to ₹827 Cr and PAT +90.1% to ₹329 Cr.

• Margins expanding: EBITDA margin improved sharply to 16.7% from 12.5%, driven by better product mix and higher capacity utilisation.

• Business mix changing: Product-led revenue rose to 62% from 42%, while private customers increased to 84% from 65%.

• Exports taking off: Export contribution jumped to 41.4% from 12.2% in FY25, with >70% of cable production now serving international markets.

• Big global win: ₹10,159 Cr ($1.1B) OFC (Optical Fiber Cable) supply agreement with a global hyperscaler. Management targets exports at >50% of revenue by FY27.

• Strong visibility: Order book stood at ₹21,206 Cr in March 2026 and increased to ₹26,665 Cr by June 2026.

• Profitability is shifting: Telecom Products generated ₹2,931 Cr revenue and ₹764 Cr segment profit, while Turnkey Contracts generated ₹1,875 Cr revenue but a ₹113 Cr loss.

• Strategic pivot working: HFCL is moving from lower-margin project execution towards higher-margin, product-led businesses.

• Capacity expansion: OF capacity targeted at 38.5 mn fkm (fiber kilometer) and OFC capacity at 56.36 mn fkm by July 2028, with ~₹580 Cr being invested in backward integration into preforms.

• Defence opportunity: Defence revenue targeted at ₹500 Cr in FY27 vs ₹77 Cr in FY26, with a ~₹2,189 Cr defence/aerospace pipeline.

• Aerospace entry: Proposed acquisition brings an export-oriented ₹1,890 Cr order book, while a 1,000-acre defence facility is being developed in Andhra Pradesh.

• BharatNet optionality: HFCL has secured >₹7,335 Cr of Phase III contracts and sees upcoming opportunities worth >₹50,000 Cr.

• R&D focus: 229 R&D professionals are working across 5G, Wi-Fi, AI-enabled networking and emerging 6G technologies.

• Balance sheet: Debt increased to ₹1,713 Cr, but Net Debt/Equity remained comfortable at 0.34x.

• Key concern - cash flow: Operating cash flow was -₹335 Cr despite ₹329 Cr PAT, mainly due to higher inventory and receivables supporting the growing order book.

Overall, FY26 marks a meaningful transformation - from projects to products, domestic to global, and telecom towards a broader connectivity + defence + aerospace platform.

PB Fintech beyond Q1 FY27 numbers 

PB Fintech’s next phase looks broader than just selling more insurance.

Health and term remain the core opportunity. New health and term premium grew 53% YoY, while 82% of customers coming to PB are new to insurance. Monthly payment options are also helping make health insurance more affordable.

Renewals could become the next earnings driver. Renewal revenue is already growing 55%, and management expects 50% growth for some time as customers acquired over the last few years start renewing.

PB Partners is expanding the opportunity offline and into smaller cities. It has 5 lakh advisors, while 78% of its premium already comes from tier 2 and 3 cities.

Paisabazaar has reached operating breakeven and is expanding beyond loans into daily SIPs, bonds, payments and PB Money. According to management, these are initially meant to increase customer engagement rather than profits.

PB Health is the biggest new bet. Two hospitals are now operational, with management targeting around ₹500 Cr annual revenue run rate and breakeven by March 2027. If it works, PB gets exposure to both health insurance and healthcare delivery.

AI is another potential lever. It already touches 30% to 40% of PB’s 10 crore monthly customer interactions and could improve sales conversion, servicing and productivity.

The key point is that management still prefers "growth over margins". Rising renewals and AI can improve profitability, but much of the benefit will be reinvested for customer growth.

The opportunity is large across insurance penetration, renewals, offline distribution and healthcare. The risks are equally clear; regulatory changes, continued high customer acquisition spending, execution in hospitals and maintaining focus across many new businesses.
